params.prompt:
One continuous nine-second eye-level fixed-camera seated wide shot of the man in the IMAGE reference. Preserve his identity, clear-framed glasses, light blue chambray button-down with the sleeves rolled to the forearm, the small country inn breakfast room with its wooden tables and chairs, soft daylight from the side window, lighting and framing with both forearms and complete hands visible on the wooden table. He sits naturally and relaxed, shoulders easy, neither stiff and upright nor slouched.

The first VIDEO supplies connected public-facing articulation to the lens. The second VIDEO supplies relaxed listening stillness and ordinary blinks. They are behavior references only. Do not copy their clothing, room, lighting, unrelated speech or mouth timing. Natural conversational body language: breathing visible in the chest and shoulders, small shoulder shifts with emphasis, and the hands lift slightly off the table for one or two small natural gestures on stressed words, then settle again. The IMAGE controls identity and setting. The AUDIO controls words, voice, cadence and pauses.

Speak only the exact 7.208333-second AUDIO reference: "I spent ten years in hospitality, including Ace Hotel and Standard Hotels. I know this business from the inside out."

Lip sync is the priority: mouth shapes match every syllable of the AUDIO precisely and close fully on the pauses. The head faces the lens with the natural small movement that speech stress causes; no repeated nod. After the last word he relaxes and settles, with no extra words.

No finger point, head shake, smirk, raised-brow performance or theatrical surprise. Keep the camera fixed and wide. No camera move, cut, zoom, caption, title, logo, music, additional person or extra objects.

Follow the AUDIO reference at its original speed and cadence. Finish speaking when the AUDIO reference ends, then settle into a relaxed resting pose for the remaining picture duration with no extra words. Do not stretch the speech to fill the generated clip.
